Protocols / Culturing & settling selection

Daily growth and settling selection

Culturing & settling selectionBy Various authorsVersion 1 · updated 2026-10-07

Standard 24 h growth in YPD followed by daily settling selection, used to propagate snowflake yeast populations.

Download (.docx) PDF

Adapted from the lab compendium Snowflake Yeast Protocols — Ratcliff Lab / MuLTEE (V2).

Growth

  1. Inoculate from the previous day’s settled fraction (see Settling selection) or from a fresh colony/stock into 10 mL fresh growth medium (YPD, per liter: 1 L water, 20 g dextrose, 20 g peptone, 10 g yeast extract, autoclaved).
  2. Grow with shaking for approximately 24 h, at 30 °C, 250 rpm.

Settling selection

  1. Vortex the culture very briefly to resuspend clusters. Do not vortex at over ~2,300 rpm.
  2. Transfer 1 mL of culture into a new tube to settle. Use a wide-bore pipette tip if working with macroscopic clusters.
  3. Settle undisturbed:
    1. Macroscopic populations: 30 seconds.
    2. Microscopic populations: 3 minutes.
  4. Remove the top 900 μL by eye without disturbing the settled pellet (pipette from above the 0.1 mL mark on the tube).
  5. Transfer 50 μL from the bottom of the remaining ~100 μL into fresh medium to start the next day’s culture (using a wide-bore pipette tip if working with macroscopic clusters).

The experiment

The Multicellularity Long-Term Evolution Experiment is run by the Ratcliff Lab in the School of Biological Sciences at the Georgia Institute of Technology.
